title: Cheap and Powerful Tests for Supervised Subspaces: Per-Component Inference for PLS
claim: A cheap per-component inference procedure chains resampled test statistics, sequential deflation with stopping, and a rotation that leaves inference unchanged.
layout: 3 panels: A top row, B vertical flowchart, C right; math in boxes
description: A three-panel flowchart in boxes and arrows. Panel A, across the top, is the inner loop. A box holding (X^(h), y^(h)) leads to a box describing J random 50/50 splits with PLS on the training half, held-out correlation and Fisher-z. That leads to a shaded blue box with the Nadeau-Bengio t-statistic formula and a p-value from t with J-1 degrees of freedom. Panel B, at lower left, is the outer loop. Three rows of (X^(h), y^(h)) boxes each feed an NB-t box and then an orange diamond testing p_h ≤ α. The first two rows end in a green check and 'reject'. The third ends in a red 'stop'. Arrows between rows are labelled 'deflate' and show the deflation equations. A joint FWER summary formula sits at the bottom. Panel C, at right, has dashed grey boxes for the varimax rotation, with an italic invariance note beneath. The palette is pale blue, orange and grey.
caption: Inference pipeline for §3.3. (A) Per-axis NB t-statistic (tNB,h, Eq. (3)): J random 50/50 splits feed Fisher-z aggregation with the corrected resampled variance. (B) Fixed-sequence FWER over NIPALS-deflated pairs (X(h), y(h)), h = 1, . . . , K∗, stopping at the first non-rejection; the joint summary α∗
abstract: Partial Least Squares (PLS) regression extracts a few outcome-aligned directions in a high-dimensional X and is widely used across applied science, but inference on the resulting fit is either expensive, biased and discouraged, or absent. We reduce inference to held-out OLS refits of the supervised subspace, a primitive shared by PLS, supervised PCA, and linear probes, and supply two tests using held-out correlations: a Nadeau-Bengio corrected asymptotic t-test as a fast approximation, and a permutation test with comparable power, finite-sample valid under outcome-predictor independence and iid rows. Held-out predictions are unchanged under any orthogonal rebasing of the supervised span, so an interpretable basis such as varimax inherits the joint claim but not a per-axis p-value; per-component claims come from a fixed-sequence test on the PLS extraction order. We validate on synthetic geometries, two NIR chemometric datasets, and cross-lingual word-embedding regressions; the exact test also transfers to supervised PCA and a ridge probe. The proposed tests have more power than CV-permutation-Q^2, at a fraction of its cost. A pre-run check on n and the spectrum of X says when the approximation is safe. We release a Rust library with Python, R, and Julia bindings, plus a Python text pipeline.
